title: Desmoothing and boundary recovery
pvg_object: replacement of a soft logarithmic valuation boundary by a hard half-space boundary
ant_object: passage from weighted Mellin sums to sharp summatory functions
forward_translation: A smooth asymptotic may be converted to a sharp one only through positivity, monotonicity, bracketing weights, partial summation, or a named desmoothing theorem with quantified boundary loss.
reverse_translation: A sharp estimate generally implies families of smooth estimates by integration, but a single smooth estimate does not reconstruct boundary concentration.
preserved_information: bulk main scales and constants when the transfer theorem certifies them
lost_information: mass concentrated near n=x and oscillation on the smoothing width
trigger: A proof deletes W from W(n/x) or claims the same sharp error term.
typical_output: a sharp theorem with an explicit boundary error or a certificate that desmoothing is unavailable
error_or_wall: Boundary mass can be as large as the proposed remainder even when the smooth average is controlled.
required_certificate: Specify the smoothing family, transition width, coefficient hypotheses, boundary estimate, and optimization producing the sharp error.
positive_example: Nonnegative coefficients and upper/lower smooth approximations can squeeze the sharp main term with a quantified transition loss.
counterexample: Deleting W from a smooth contour formula preserves neither the kernel nor the error term.
anti_overclaim: Smooth and sharp statements are separate theorems unless a transfer certificate is supplied.
source_basis: Classical Mellin, Perron, partial summation, and Tauberian transfer

title: Tauberian hypotheses and converse limits
pvg_object: growth of weighted lattice mass as a size half-space expands
ant_object: boundary behavior of a Dirichlet or Mellin transform and a Tauberian conclusion
forward_translation: Route to a named Tauberian theorem only after matching coefficient sign, monotonicity, continuation, boundary regularity, and growth hypotheses.
reverse_translation: A summatory asymptotic may suggest a singularity, but a converse statement requires its own theorem and need not recover the full analytic continuation.
preserved_information: the main asymptotic information guaranteed by the matched theorem
lost_information: secondary terms, vertical behavior, and unique reconstruction of the transform
trigger: A proof infers a sharp asymptotic from boundary behavior or infers a pole from an asymptotic.
typical_output: a theorem-name and hypothesis ledger or a refusal at the boundary
error_or_wall: Near-boundary control weaker than the theorem requires invalidates the transfer; converse implications are especially nonunique.
required_certificate: Cite the exact Tauberian or converse theorem and verify every sign, regularity, boundary, and normalization assumption.
positive_example: Ikehara-type transfer uses nonnegative coefficients and controlled behavior on Re(s)=1.
counterexample: A visible x^a log x term alone does not uniquely reconstruct a double pole and residual factor.
anti_overclaim: Tauberian language cannot replace hypothesis matching.

title: Vertical-strip growth and contour-edge certificate
pvg_object: transport of valuation-weighted mass across a complex scaling contour
ant_object: meromorphic continuation on a strip, polynomial vertical growth, horizontal-edge decay, and control of the shifted line
forward_translation: A contour shift requires a four-part certificate: continuation in the rectangle, pole inventory, vertical growth offset by kernel decay, and an integrable bound on the new line.
reverse_translation: A valid residue formula records that these analytic controls existed, but the formula alone does not reconstruct their uniform constants.
preserved_information: which poles are crossed and the analytic region supporting the transfer
lost_information: hidden strip constants and parameter dependence unless recorded
trigger: Mellin or Perron contours are moved and horizontal integrals are declared negligible.
typical_output: a complete contour rectangle certificate with explicit dependence
error_or_wall: Kernel decay cannot compensate for an analytic factor whose growth was never bounded.
required_certificate: State strip continuation, polynomial growth exponent, kernel decay order, horizontal limits, and the absolute bound on the new vertical integral.
positive_example: If the analytic factor grows like (1+|t|)^A, choose Mellin decay order N>A+2.
counterexample: Saying smoothness handles the contour without an L-function growth bound leaves a proof gap.
anti_overclaim: Contour pictures do not prove edge decay.
